summary_en: ITG-G Holdings raised the tender offer price to 2,655 yen per share and the self-acquisition price to 2,113 yen per share on November 11, 2026. The special committee rejected a competing proposal from candidate B, determined it does not qualify as a superior proposal under the acquisition agreement, and initiated a Best & Final process requiring all candidates to submit final bids simultaneously.
title_en: Notice of Partial Amendment to 'Opinion Statement Supporting and Recommendation to Tender Shares in Response to Public Tender Offer by ITG-G Holdings Inc. for Our Shares' (Change Notification)
translation_en_brief:
On November 11, 2026, ITG-G Holdings increased its tender offer price to 2,655 yen per share and the self-acquisition price to 2,113 yen per share. Following receipt of a competing proposal from candidate B through Mitsui & Co., the special committee re-evaluated the offer. The committee determined that candidate B's proposal does not contribute to enhancement of the company's corporate value and does not qualify as a superior proposal under the acquisition agreement, and therefore rejected any participation in a process involving B's bid.

Concerned that incremental price increases and repeated extensions of the tender offer period would prolong uncertainty and damage the company's business operations and corporate value, the special committee implemented a Best & Final process. This process invited all qualified candidates—founders and Integral (representing the initial bidder), candidate C, and supporters Mitsui & Co. and Mitsubishi Corporation—to submit their final and best proposals simultaneously on equal terms. The committee received responses on November 18, 2026, with the initial bidder and Integral agreeing to participate subject to certain conditions, while candidate C declined and the two sponsors indicated conditional willingness to cooperate.

Candidate B was excluded from the Best & Final process because: (i) its proposal does not advance corporate value; (ii) the company has consistently rejected B's proposals and required compliance with standstill obligations under the confidentiality agreement; and (iii) B lacks the qualification to submit a superior proposal under the acquisition agreement, and the company is contractually prohibited from soliciting non-public transaction proposals from B.
